title: Keep pre-rollout samples out of the canary's first window

blocks.text: The canary analysis compares latency before and after a rollout. Every latency sample is stamped with its offset in milliseconds from the moment the rollout started, so samples taken before it have negative offsets, and they are counted in fixed windows held in a small ring of slots.

Three things are wrong on the dashboard: the old version's last slow samples show up in the new version's first window, recording any sample from before the rollout throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, and a window shows 0% slow unless every sample in it was slow.
`SampleWindows` already records and reports. Finish the three `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/SampleWindows.java`:

items: `window(offsetMs)`: the window a sample falls in, as its comment defines it;
`slot(window)`: the slot that holds a window's counts;
`slowPercent(slow, total)`: the share of slow samples, as a whole percentage rounded down.

cases.says: samples taken after the rollout are counted in the right window and slot, and an all-slow or all-fast window reports 100 or 0
a sample with a small negative offset falls in window -1, not in window 0
every window, negative ones included, maps to a slot from 0 to slots - 1, and consecutive windows use consecutive slots
a partly slow window reports its percentage rounded down, not 0

origin.section: Integer Division Truncates Toward Zero, and % Takes the Sign of the Dividend

concepts: Integer / discards the fraction, so a percentage computed as part / whole * 100 is 0 until part reaches whole; multiplying first keeps it.
% takes the sign of the dividend, so a negative left operand gives a negative remainder and a negative index; Math.floorMod takes the divisor's sign.
Integer / rounds toward zero, so a small negative offset falls in the same bucket as a small positive one; Math.floorDiv rounds toward negative infinity.
